newsitem.title: INDIA: India to raise 5 bln rupees in 96/97 by share sale.
newsitem.headline: India to raise 5 bln rupees in 96/97 by share sale.

text.p: India expects to raise five billion rupees ($140 million) in 1996/97 (April-March) through the sale of partial stakes in state-owned firms against a target of 50 billion, budget documents showed on Friday.
The documents were released after Finance Minister P. Chidambaram presented the 1997/98 federal budget to parliament.

India has planned to sell a seven percent stake in telecommunications firm Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) and five percent in crude oil refining company Indian Oil Corp (IOC) in the first round of divestment in 1996/97.
But the government has not yet fixed a date for the selloff. The 1996/97 fiscal year ends on March 31.
Chidambaram told lawmakers the government expects to take in 48 billion rupees from the sale of government stakes in state-controlled firms in 1997/98.

The government plans to sell some of its shares in three state-controlled firms -- Gas Authority of India Ltd, Modern Food Industries (India) Ltd and the India Tourism Development Corp -- as suggested by the Disinvestment Commission, Chidambaram added.
The Disinvestment Commission was set up last year by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government to advise on privatisation of state-firms.
The government raised 3.57 billion rupees from divestment in 1995/96, well short of its target of 70 billion.
